16.3 Run Property 15 against the **unmod.failingExample:
Property 15 baseline against the UNMODIFIED tree — three breach classes, exactly as design §5.4 predicts.

RENDERED ARM (index.html, 24 pills x 4 viewports; homepage geometry is the only one with rendered instances):
  c5w  label width / border-box width — 0.877 @320 (pass), 0.883 @768, 0.883 @1024, 0.884 @1440
       vs the 0.88 ceiling. BREACH at 768/1024/1440. "Waterjet fabrication".
       (design predicted 0.891-0.893; measured 0.884 worst case)
  c2   vertical symmetry — 6.66px @320, 7.55px @768/1024, 8.41px @1440 vs the 1px tolerance.
       BREACH at all four viewports, all 24 pills. gapTop ~2.4px / gapBottom ~10.8px @1440:
       min-height 1.7rem (27.2px) exceeds the 19.12px content height and block layout drops
       all the slack below the line box. (design predicted ~8.1px; measured 8.41px)

DECLARED ARM (body.home #main .button.skills, body.home #main .actions .button — the
wider-context geometry, which has ZERO rendered instances, see the finding recorded in
pill-geometry.mjs):
  c5h  line box height / border-box height = 1.000 vs the 0.85 ceiling. BREACH.
  c4   horizontal padding / effective vertical gap = Infinity (gap = 0) vs 1.5-3.5. BREACH.
       Cause: line-height: 2.25rem is a LENGTH set equal to height: 2.25rem.
  c5w  0.831 (widest) / 0.424 (narrowest) — pass, and identical to §5.4's table.

Label box is read from a text-node Range via getClientRects(), expanded to the resolved
line-height about its centre. A pass here would mean the label box was being read from the
anchor rect instead — the anchor IS the pill, so every ratio would be 1.000.
